items.stem: Which best distinguishes an output from a benefit?

options.text: An output is what is delivered; a benefit is the measurable improvement it enables
options.rationale: Correct: outputs are deliverables, benefits are the value realised from them.

options.text: They are two words for the same thing
options.rationale: They are distinct concepts in benefits management.

options.text: An output is always financial, a benefit never is
options.rationale: Both can be financial or non-financial.

options.text: A benefit is delivered before the output
options.rationale: Benefits are realised after and because of outputs.

items.explanation: Correct: outputs are deliverables, benefits are the value realised from them.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are needed to measure a benefit credibly? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A baseline of the current state
options.rationale: Correct: without a baseline you cannot show change.

options.text: A defined measure and target with a date
options.rationale: Correct: a measurable target makes realisation verifiable.

options.text: A promise that it will be 'much better'

options.rationale: Opinion is not an objective measure.

items.explanation: Correct: without a baseline you cannot show change.

options.text: A business role accountable for realising the benefit after delivery
options.rationale: Correct: benefit ownership usually sits with the business, not the project team.

options.text: The project manager, who owns it forever
options.rationale: PMs usually hand benefit ownership to the business.

options.text: Whoever happens to be free that week
options.rationale: Ownership must be deliberate and accountable.

items.explanation: Correct: benefit ownership usually sits with the business, not the project team.
